summary: One required finding: preserve the defined bare/suffixed key formats instead of requiring a subject on every unchanged syntax key. One non-blocking clarification names the empty arrays in a successful no-group candidate result. The outcome law, ERROR exception, schema copies and structural binding otherwise check out.

requiredFindings.problem: The new route requires every key to carry a colon-suffixed subject, but three of the unchanged §1.2 emissions are bare keys. A grammar-version mismatch currently emits native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest without any suffix; bundle and normalizer membership failures do likewise. Those outputs cannot satisfy the new universal subject rule while LD-6 keeps NEM and its selected B-S9 copies unchanged. The new missing-closure key is also given no subject value. The 25-key audit proves prefix coverage, not this output-format obligation.

evidence.text: Each key carries its colon-suffixed subject, and the refusals are one sorted set.
Literal append calls emit native.syntax-grammar-version-not-from-manifest, native.syntax-grammar-bundle-not-in-closure and native.syntax-normalizer-spec-not-in-closure without a colon or subject.
The selected B-S9 reference preserves the same three bare emissions. Source inspection and AST parsing confirm the strings without importing the model.
The §1.2 checks and both selected native-model copies are intentionally unchanged.
The audit extracts native.syntax-* prefixes and compares sets; it does not compare the emitted bare/suffixed forms.

fix.instruction: Preserve the existing §1.2 emission formats and define the new absence key explicitly, rather than introducing an unrecorded NEM change. Apply the following exact replacement in the NE:3530 after string, carry it through the builder and PASSAGES.md, and refresh the record and subject pins. Check the inherited bare forms as well as key-prefix membership in the read-only evidence.

exactReplacement.before: Each key carries its colon-suffixed subject, and the refusals are one sorted set.
exactReplacement.after: Keys retain their defined subject form: existing §1.2 keys are unchanged, and item 5's admission-chain keys use that item's subjects where specified. `native.syntax-grammar-closure-absent` is emitted without a subject suffix. The refusals are one sorted set.

nonBlockingObservations.problem: The successful no-group sentence says empty arrays without naming them. A nonempty census that parses successfully but produces no clone group must keep examinedPaths equal to the census; only groupDigests and sourceBodies are empty. The preceding sentence and the later examinedPaths rule already specify the correct behavior, so this is a non-blocking wording clarification.

evidence.text: The successful empty-result row keeps examinedPaths equal to the census, with groupDigests and sourceBodies empty.
For state complete, examinedPaths must equal the candidate extent; otherwise admission records EXECUTION_INPUTS_CANDIDATE_BIND.

fix.instruction: Name the empty arrays explicitly in the NE:306 text and its generated mirrors.

exactReplacement.before: An explicit `[]` census, and a successful result with no group, are `complete` with empty arrays;
exactReplacement.after: An explicit `[]` census is `complete` with `examinedPaths: []`, `groupDigests: []` and `sourceBodies: []`. A successful result with no group is `complete` with `examinedPaths` equal to the census, `groupDigests: []` and `sourceBodies: []`;

decisionChecks.detail: The four outcomes, whole-file prohibition on salvaged facts/bodies, invalid-UTF-8 handling, identity-bearing size/work/node/depth bounds, native crash residual, and Coverage precedence match E1 items 10, 11 and 18. wasm-only memory/trap/module behavior is marked inactive. clones-near has no Coverage; its complete/partial cases, unsupported census paths, parsed-only examinedPaths, one precedence-selected pair, no-envelope fault/cancellation rule, and whole-group digest-prefix retention including the 100,000-body union match item 14a. Explicit empty census and successful no-group results remain distinct. Byte layout is correctly left to E2a.

65535 is the correct reserved visible ERROR symbol, outside the grammar table; 65534 is the hidden ERROR_REPEAT and is not admitted as a visible node. Pinned runtime node.c defines ts_node_is_error as ts_node_symbol == ts_builtin_sym_error; parser.h and language.h define the two reserved symbols; language.c gives ERROR visible metadata and ERROR_REPEAT hidden metadata. The pinned Rust binding accepts ids >=65534 for reserved lookup, not as proof that ERROR_REPEAT is visible. The E0 report supplies two independent serializers, 8,351 identical trees and 41 syntax-error files. This supports LD-2, while future E2b must enforce the newly explicit agreement rule; E0 is not production qualification.

decisionChecks.result: REQUIRED-FINDING RF-SYN1-1; key set and routing otherwise PASS
decisionChecks.detail: All 25 prefixes are present: 11 existing model keys, 13 E1 chain keys including normalization-map-mismatch, and one missing-closure key. Seven chain keys apply to both branches, build-mismatch only to native, and five module/ABI/symbol-table keys only to inactive wasm. Missing or statically inadmissible grammar context correctly refuses before PlanId with request-rejected / REQUEST.PRECONDITION_FAILED; no alternate parser or partial universe is substituted. The added absence key distinguishes no closure from a missing member of an existing closure. Its subject form and inherited bare keys need RF-SYN1-1.

The row uses E1 item 10 and the already-selected host-invariant fault cause: operational-failed / 4 / SYSTEM.OUTCOME.ILLEGAL_STATE / HOST.INVARIANT_VIOLATED, subject native.syntax-backend-fault:<grammarId>. It produces no Coverage, candidate envelope or Run and is never retried. Native parser abort/stack/allocator failures are expressly not claimed as typed returns. X-J1 is the right owner route: widen row 52 at J-epsilon and add a backend-fault row before J2a/outcomes.rs projects these new conditions. Unregistered native keys remain operational-record detail, without adding DomainDetailCode members.

Each complete copy has only the two code-point-ordered source-parse-error insertions plus the input-closure-incomplete rule restatement. The design/product relation is preserved byte for byte; product base equals the pinned product parent. No bound JSON override is lost. NativeCause description, all other allowedCauses lists, DeficiencyV2, UnavailableReasonV3 and startup bytes remain unchanged. Startup reason enums are separate negotiated vocabularies and Coverage references the native owner by URN. Joint binding/materialization with SYN-1F preserves the foundation cause mirrors.

decisionChecks.detail: The cause-carrier logic reads the data registry and restates no NativeCause list. The old D9_MAP does not attempt total coverage of native-context admission keys, and the execution-chain checks belong to E2b. No NEM logic edit or byte-identical model successor is warranted for the new cause itself. RF-SYN1-1 removes the new output-format demand that otherwise contradicts retaining the existing emissions. Reference execution must use the selected successor schema data; this review did not import or run NEM.

Real verify_design accepts SYN-1 alone at cd5958b (82 to 83), the proposed chain SYN-1 / CRC-1 / SYN-1F / SYN-NS (82 to 86), and the current checkout with 40 generation and 48 admission sources plus 15 aliases verified. The three parents, five untouched line selectors, ten candidates and eleven subject members are structurally valid. Inventory and inheritance remain unchanged. Synthetic standalone acceptance proves eligibility only; actual binding must remain joint with SYN-1F as LD-11 requires, after real independent review and root assent.
